dates.notes: Issued by G20 ministers at the Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, on 2 September 2026. The text is a ministerial deliverable accompanying the G20 Innovation Ministerial Statement; it is not a leaders' communiqué or a treaty.

gaps: Non-binding: it creates no legal obligation, ratification, depositary, monitoring or enforcement.
No itemised list of endorsing States is published; the text is a ministerial deliverable of the G20 presidency.
The companion AI Prosperity Compact is a voluntary private-sector partnership pledge, not an intergovernmental instrument, and is not counted as a separate record here.
The objectives focus on AI skills and workforce development, not on AI safety, liability or market access.
No full text, citable units or original file is stored in this record; it is metadata-only.

issuer.name: G20 Innovation Ministers, Chapel Hill, North Carolina

legal_nature.rationale: A ministerial deliverable adopted at a G20 Innovation Ministerial. It is a political text with voluntary objectives; it has no signature, ratification, depositary or entry-into-force clause and creates no legal obligation.

provenance.discovered_via: US Department of Commerce G20 Innovation Ministerial pages; the G20 deliverables had been recorded as pending in the candidate register, but the objectives were adopted on 2 September 2026.

related.note: The objectives acknowledge the G20's prior AI work, including the G20 AI Principles, which are the OECD AI Principles as endorsed.
A parallel G7 AI deliverable; the G20 text is workforce-focused and non-binding, while the G7 code is addressed to AI developers.
Both address AI capacity-building, but the G20 text is a ministerial political deliverable rather than a UN resolution.

ai_provisions: Nine voluntary objectives on AI skills, AI literacy, apprenticeships, technical training, lifelong learning and workforce readiness.
Commitments to expand access to AI education and hands-on technical training, including through public-private partnerships.
Encouragement of voluntary information sharing on workforce development and AI adoption.
Reference to the G20's prior AI work and to human-centric, reliable approaches to AI adoption.
relevance.excluded_scope: A non-binding ministerial text on AI workforce development. It does not create AI safety, testing, liability or market-access rules and establishes no monitoring mechanism.
relevance.reason: The G20 AI Prosperity Objectives are an adopted AI-specific ministerial text from September 2026 and were still marked as pending in the corpus. Leaving them out would have repeated the omission the source-family review was meant to catch: a current instrument absent because an earlier search had stopped at the Innovation Ministerial Statement.
